At Dyer, the demand for fast answers landed on the phones. Answering them was the biggest problem in Dyer's service departments, Holmes says, so Dyer brought in AI answering from an AI product.

Holmes now calls the system "one of the worst things we did." The team had lost touch with its customers, Holmes says, and the system gave Dyer no read on how callers were feeling. Retention was slipping, and advisors were overwhelmed.

Sofia Gonzalez, who manages the BDC that Dyer calls its customer care department, saw the same gap. Gonzalez suspects the first provider didn't account for who Dyer's customers are: people who like a personal touch.
After the first AI product, the team was wary of another new program. A lot of the advisors, service managers, and BDC agents had the same reaction, Gonzalez says: "here we go again."

Numa sent trainers to work with people one-on-one in the store, and Holmes counts that among the biggest reasons the second try took hold. The first provider had handed over the system with no training. "Boom. Hope it works for you," in Holmes's words. "I think we got more training from Numa than we did when we installed a new CRM," Holmes says.
Gonzalez credits the on-site training, along with a better product, with turning the team's reaction around. The rollout went much the same way in all the stores, Holmes says.
Holmes had expected advisors to see Numa as one more process to fit into the day. Advisors and managers came back with a different question, Holmes says: "why didn't we have this before?"
Numa also comes up in Dyer's daily reports and weekly meetings. Holmes says the team reviews its Numa number there, alongside gross profit and the other metrics Dyer tracks.

Dyer hires service advisors for "that tenacity to sell," Holmes says, but before Numa those advisors were "spending 30, 40% of their time on the phones." Holmes put the problem as a question: "Why do we have someone with that personality, the made-to-sell, spending all their time answering phones?"

Holmes says call volume has come down since the team could see who had heard back. Advisors can concentrate on selling. Some of the time that went to the phones now goes to multi-point videos, and Dyer sends more of them to customers.
"It's increased CSI, it's increased NPS, it's increased customer satisfaction, increased gross profit, and employee retention."
